subject: Clarify measurement epoch & transient-noise policy for hosted latency SLOs
messages:
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@firmbyte.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ops@firmbyte.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify hosted API measurement for p50/p95 — carveouts during traffic anomalies

Sergio / Lauren,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week. As we scope the PoC we need clarity on how Redwood measures the p50 and p95 latency commitments for the hosted API. A few concrete points from our side:

- We run seasonal traffic bursts during marketing sends; transient spikes can push p95 above thresholds for short windows.
- For an enterprise SLA we'd like to understand if Redwood provides any transient/noise carveouts (for example, exceptions for short-term bursts), how evidence is submitted, and what limits (frequency, duration) are applied.
- Also need to confirm the measurement epoch (rolling 28d vs calendar month) and whether regional routing differences are reflected in the SLA.

Attached is a short request doc (FirmByte_SLA_RQ.pdf) with our baseline traffic patterns. Can you propose a measurement policy we can use for the contract? If you can also include the operational evidence we'd need to qualify an exclusion that would be ideal.

Best,
Alex
Alex Grant
Head of Infrastructure — FirmByte
Attach: FirmByte_SLA_RQ.pdf

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@firmbyte.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API measurement for p50/p95 — carveouts during traffic anomalies

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. I ran this by infra and product and put together a short proposal attached (measurement-proposal-v1.pdf). High level summary inline below so the PoC team has something to review quickly.

TL;DR proposal (recommended):
- Measurement epoch: 28-day rolling window, computed at regional level (us/eu/apac). Rolling window ensures the sample reflects recent traffic patterns while avoiding month boundary artifacts.
- Quantiles: p50 measured across all requests; p95 computed from sampled request latencies with 100% sampling for routed production traffic (no downsampling for SLOs).
- Transient-noise exclusion (limited carveout):
  - Trigger conditions: sudden traffic >10x baseline sustained for <= 3 hours OR known external event (e.g., partner API outage) with timeline evidence.
  - Evidence: request-level traces (KV cache hit rates, request ids), ingress traffic graphs, and an ops postmortem or vendor report.
  - Limits: at most 2 carveouts per rolling 90-day period per account, each carveout can cover up to 3 hours of measurement time.
- Operational path: customer opens a "Burst Exception" request via the HubSpot deal page; engineering will triage within 48 hours and, if approved, apply a temporary carveout to the epoch and notify customer.

We kept the carveout small to avoid masking sustained regressions while still giving breathing room for clearly external/short events. I've attached the full proposal with examples and the exact telemetry we need.

Next steps: if that looks reasonable we can (1) include the language in a PoC addendum, (2) create the HubSpot workflow for exception intake, and (3) ask your team for the evidence package template.

Attaching: measurement-proposal-v1.pdf

— Sergio
Sergio Álvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@firmbyte.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 14:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API measurement for p50/p95 — carveouts during traffic anomalies

Alex / Sergio — quick product note to clarify implementation details so legal/ops can sign off cleanly.

- Regional measurement: we report p50/p95 per-region and then aggregate for the contract. The contract will list the region(s) covered and the primary region for SLO calculation.
- Sampling and telemetry: for SLOs we keep full sampling for latency metrics but use artifact tagging (route_id, customer_id, model_variant) so the exclusion can be scoped to traffic that matches the incident signature.
- Burst detection algorithm (for carveout eligibility): we use a baseline defined as a 7d median traffic volume; a burst is 10x that median for >= 5 minutes. For the policy above, we only allow carveouts for bursts that persist beyond 30 minutes and are remediated within 3 hours.
- Credits & limits: product recommends limiting service-credit exposure — we propose a maximum of 10% invoice credit per quarter tied to approved carveouts. Marissa: flagging you for customer credit policy approval.

If this aligns I can add the paragraph to the PoC addendum and push the HubSpot intake form. Also need to confirm if FirmByte wants regional-only coverage (us) or global.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Management — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Grant <alex.grant@firmbyte.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API measurement for p50/p95 — carveouts during traffic anomalies

Thanks team — reviewed the proposal. Approve conditional exception flow with the following constraints:

1) Carveouts are discretionary and require the full evidence package and ops sign-off. No automatic exclusions.
2) Cap credits tied to carveouts at a 10% quarterly maximum as Lauren suggested; any larger credit requires VP approval.
3) Limit of two carveouts per 90d per account; each carveout max 3 hours.
4) Require a runbook and post-incident review within 7 days. Ops to publish a runbook draft (runbook-draft.odt) before start of PoC.

Sergio — please add the agreed language to the PoC addendum and create the HubSpot intake (link to follow). Also add the specific telemetry list (trace ids, ingress graphs, KV hit rates) to the evidence template.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
Attach: runbook-draft.odt
